# 1.1 · Dot, Matvec, Matmul

`Level 1: Numbers That Learn` · `+10 XP` · `drill 1 of 3`

## The job
Write four functions on plain lists: `dot(a, b)`, `matvec(M, v)`, `transpose(M)` and
`matmul(A, B)`. A vector is a list of numbers; a matrix is a list of rows. Mismatched
shapes raise `ValueError` instead of quietly producing garbage.

## Why it matters
A dense layer in a neural network is `matvec(weights, inputs)` plus a bias. Attention is
two matmuls and a softmax. Most "the model outputs nonsense" bugs you will ever chase are
shape bugs, so the habit of refusing bad shapes loudly starts here.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 1.1     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 1.1      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. `zip(a, b)` walks two lists in lockstep. Check the lengths first, because zip silently stops at the shorter one.
2. `matvec` is one `dot` per row of the matrix.
3. `transpose` turns columns into rows: `zip(*M)` hands you the columns as tuples.
4. `matmul(A, B)[i][j]` is the dot of row i of A with column j of B. Transposing B first makes the columns easy to reach.

</details>
